clue.text: Mobster's gun reportedly carried by the sod making a call for global harmony

indicators.note: reportedly tells us to take the sound of the gangster's word rather than its spelling

parts.note: a piece is gangster slang for a handgun
a thing carried by something is on it
sod is turf, the earth itself

explanation.surface: A gangster with a pistol somehow ends up appealing for world peace, a seasonal irony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' means PIECE said aloud, giving PEACE; 'carried by' gives ON and 'the sod' EARTH. The answer runs across 1 and 12.
explanation.definitionFit: The angels' Christmas message wishes tranquillity across the whole world, hence a plea for worldwide concord.

clue.text: A short and curly presiding officer pursuing local interest

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so this piece comes last

parts.note: a local is a British pub, the one nearest your home
I is the abbreviation for interest in finance formulas
the chair presides over a meeting

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of a committee chair poking into parish affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursuing' puts the presiding officer last. 'Short and curly' is British slang from 'to have someone by the short and curlies'; 'local interest' looks like parish concerns but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Body hair in the groin is famously short and curly, the source of the slang phrase.

clue.text: Word confused with 'Harry penetrating a sheep'

indicators.note: penetrating means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
to harry someone is to nag them

explanation.surface: A rude misunderstanding about Harry and a sheep, typical Private Eye smut.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry is a verb here, not a name: NAG goes 'penetrating' A RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A word whose letters have been jumbled into a new order is exactly what this puzzle term names.

clue.text: Regular lay taken by The Vicar?

parts.note: regular and even both mean steady and uniform
a lay is an old word for a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A smutty hint that the vicar enjoys a regular romp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like slang for sex but is a poetic word for a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening prayer in the Church of England is a service a parish priest conducts.

clue.text: New fancy limo and sex without restriction …

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine, so the letters are made into something new

parts.note: it is a coy slang word for sex

explanation.surface: A flashy new limousine and unrestrained sex: a tabloid fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' reworks LIMO into OLIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning there is no cap or boundary at all, as with unlimited spending.

clue.text: Paula Yates's marks for soldiers' performances?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: inked designs on the skin, which the TV presenter Paula Yates sported
second meaning: a military tattoo is an outdoor display by soldiers

explanation.walkthrough: Paula Yates was a British TV presenter known for her body art; a tattoo is also a military show such as the Edinburgh Tattoo.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both ink designs on skin and massed military band displays.

clue.text: … Bill, like, getting a little firm — sauce!

parts.note: a tab is a bill run up at a bar
as means like, in comparisons
Co is the short form of company, a firm

explanation.surface: Continues 4: someone, like, getting a firmer bill and some cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' looks like cheek, but it is the hot pepper condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiery Louisiana pepper condiment is a well-known brand of hot sauce.

clue.text: See 15
Iran too 'foreign' for this provincial place?

indicators.note: foreign suggests the letters are turned into something strange, a reworking

explanation.surface: Is Iran too exotic a place for a country bumpkin?
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges IRAN TOO. 'provincial' usually means rustic, but here it is literal: a Canadian province.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is divided into provinces, and this is its most populous one.

clue.text: Fergie's first rash move: accepting head from accountant

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other
move tells us to shift the letters of rash about
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of accountant is A

explanation.surface: The Duchess of York making a hasty move with help from her money man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' rearranges RASH to SRAH, which goes 'accepting' A, the 'head from' accountant. Fergie is Sarah Ferguson, Duchess of York.
explanation.definitionFit: Fergie's first name, the given name of the former Duchess of York.

clue.text: Blast Tony, say?

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the name and hear another word

parts.note: Tony Blair, the Labour leader and later Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A curse on Tony Blair, or an order to blow him up.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud harsh noise, like a trumpet's, is a synonym of a blast.

clue.text: Freer, old-style politician: "Brenda has one by flipping balls"

parts.note: Lib is short for an old Liberal, a party merged away in 1988
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, ER
a means one

indicators.note: flipping turns a word over, so its letters run the other way

parts.note: rot and balls both mean nonsense

explanation.surface: A politician quoting gossip that the Queen has a flipping pair of balls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns ROT into TOR. Brenda is the Queen in Private Eye, so ER (Elizabeth Regina).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sets others free, a freer, is a liberator.

clue.text: Archer's is most stupid bloomer of the season

indicators.note: stupid suggests muddled thinking, so these letters come out in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A dig at Jeffrey Archer, novelist and Tory peer, making the season's most stupid gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' rearranges all thirteen letters of ARCHER'S IS MOST. A 'bloomer' is also a blunder, which fits the Archer jibe; here it is a flower. The answer runs across 11 and 18.
explanation.definitionFit: A hellebore that flowers in midwinter, so it is the plant blossoming in the festive season.

clue.text: See 1
Shot of Naomi in tum surgery

indicators.note: surgery reshapes a body, so the letters are operated on and rearranged

parts.note: tum is short for tummy, and its letters are taken as written

explanation.surface: Naomi Campbell, the supermodel, having a tummy tuck.
explanation.walkthrough: The copy reads 'turn', a misreading of 'tum' (tummy): 'surgery' rearranges NAOMI IN TUM. 'Shot' looks like a photo of the model, but it is bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot in the sense of bullets or pellets fired from guns is a synonym of ammunition.

clue.text: The president's in furniture store getting end away

indicators.note: getting one's end away is slang for having sex; here it says the last letter is taken off

parts.note: Ikea is the Swedish flat-pack furniture chain

explanation.surface: A US president having a fling in a furniture showroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting end away' takes the final A off IKEA. Ike was the nickname of President Dwight D. Eisenhower.
explanation.definitionFit: Eisenhower, the 34th US president, was universally known by this nickname.

clue.text: Fare on Boxing Day horrifies trippers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the leftover roast bird eaten the day after Christmas
second meaning: abrupt drug withdrawal, dreaded by drug users

explanation.walkthrough: Boxing Day is 26 December, a British holiday; 'trippers' are drug takers, not day-trippers.
explanation.definitionFit: Unheated leftover poultry is the classic meal the day after Christmas, and the same phrase names sudden withdrawal from drugs.

clue.text: Did he come to be lying in this?

definitions.text: Did he come to be lying in this?

parts.words: Did he come to be lying in this?
parts.note: a crude cryptic definition: after sex, the wet place on the sheet is where one lies

explanation.walkthrough: 'Come' is sexual slang, and the question asks where one ends up lying afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A moist spot on bedding, left after lovemaking, is something one may find oneself lying on.

clue.text: For those who play with themselves — cool!

definitions.text: For those who play with themselves
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a card game for one player
second meaning: calm forbearance, keeping one's cool

explanation.walkthrough: Solitaire card games are called by this name in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a one-player card game and also calm endurance without losing one's temper.

clue.text: See 11
He found the right Xmas spirit: "Score and go get pissed!"

definitions.text: He found the right Xmas spirit

indicators.note: to get pissed is British slang for getting drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice for the festive season: grab some booze and go get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get pissed' rearranges SCORE and GO. Dickens's miser in A Christmas Carol is visited by spirits until he learns to keep Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's miser is reformed at the end of A Christmas Carol and embraces festive goodwill.

clue.text: PM's lies about restricting agents — something he's practised in

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so one piece holds the other
about suggests moving things around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency, a body of agents

explanation.surface: A dig at a Prime Minister lying about spies, a skill he has mastered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges PM'S LIES into SPELISM, and 'restricting' sets the agents inside it. 'about' reads like 'concerning' in the surface, which hides its job.
explanation.definitionFit: A field one is trained or expert in is one's speciality or area of expertise.

clue.text: Her hubby tense when Brenda turns up with love potion?

parts.note: the Queen's husband was Prince Philip, Phil for short
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, ER

explanation.surface: Prince Philip tense when the Queen appears with an aphrodisiac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her' points forward to Brenda, the Queen, whose husband was Philip; ER 'turns up' to give RE at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A magic drink meant to make someone fall in love is an old word for a love drug.

clue.text: Parrot in tins makes savoury snacks

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: cans are tins
to parrot is to ape, copy someone

explanation.surface: Canned parrot as a cocktail-party nibble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' is a verb here, not the bird: APE goes 'in' CANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Small savoury bites on bread or crackers, served with drinks at parties.

clue.text: Criminal in Pentonville gallery

indicators.note: in says the answer is sitting within these words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words: letters 8-14 of 'Pentonville gallery'

explanation.surface: A prisoner up in the gallery of Pentonville, a London jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlawful acts are criminal, so the adjective is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Carol's mum getting thing out

parts.note: mum means saying nothing, as in keep mum

indicators.note: out suggests something out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Carol's mother getting something out, a domestic scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol looks like a woman's name but is a Christmas song; 'mum' means SILENT, not mother, and 'out' rearranges THING into NIGHT. The answer runs across 24 and 28.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known Christmas hymn, 'Stille Nacht', sung every December.

clue.text: Royal favourite inspiring lecherous outburst by George!

parts.note: cor! is the British leer of a man ogling someone
GI stands for George I, the king written with his regnal number

explanation.surface: A lusty cry of 'Cor!' from a king named George.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cor!' is British slang for an impressed exclamation. The Queen famously kept a pack of these Welsh dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Elizabeth II was devoted to this short-legged Welsh breed, the dog most linked to the monarchy.

clue.text: Conservative leader's talk brings tears to the eyes!

parts.note: C, the first letter of Conservative, plus its S
gas is idle talk, chatter

explanation.surface: A Tory leader's speech is so moving, or so bad, it makes you cry.
explanation.definitionFit: The riot-control irritant makes eyes stream, so it is what makes people weep.

clue.text: Greer's associated with Phil's circle (Rubbish — see me. Ed)

definitions.note: Ed is short for the editor, here Private Eye's own

parts.note: Ian Greer was the lobbyist behind Ian Greer Associates, caught up in the 1990s cash-for-questions affair

indicators.note: rubbish describes a mess, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: a circle is the letter O by its shape

explanation.surface: A teacher's red-pen verdict on an essay: rubbish, see me.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Greer was a lobbyist; 'associated with' points to his firm Ian Greer Associates. 'Rubbish' rearranges PHIL'S and O into HISLOP. The bracket is a joke signed by the magazine's editor.
explanation.definitionFit: The satirist has been editor of the magazine Private Eye since 1986, the Eye's own Ed.

clue.text: Traditional Xmas fare on stage for the advancement of the Nazi

parts.note: roast goose was the traditional Christmas dinner
a step is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: A pantomime-style Christmas show staged for a Nazi's career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on stage' suggests a panto, but 'on' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The stiff-legged march of Nazi troops is a way of moving forward on parade.

clue.text: See 24
Crumbling respect held by Brenda

indicators.note: crumbling means falling to pieces, so the letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: Respect for the Queen is crumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbling' rearranges RESPECT. Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The ornamental staff a monarch carries at the coronation as a symbol of sovereignty.

clue.text: Appropriate, Tony's opening hospital — what a bomber

parts.note: to appropriate is to steal

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of Tony is T
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Tony Blair opening a hospital, then a jibe about bombing.
explanation.definitionFit: A radar-evading aircraft is a stealth bomber, so the word completes the phrase.
